studies.label: Supervised college-student mathematical creativity experiment

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 45), Participants, opening sentence; initial allocation and withdrawals discussed on PDF p. 4 (printed p. 42), Procedure

arms.name: Experimental (task resolution with ChatGPT)
arms.description: Students solved the mathematical creativity tasks with ChatGPT on personal computers, with technical training and structured example, heuristic, task-reminder, critical-thinking and divergent-thinking prompts. They could ask for solutions and refinements. PDF pp. 5-7 (printed pp. 43-45), Procedure, Figures 1-2 and Table 1. The explicit arm total appears only in Figure 1 and is left null under the figure-only rule.

arms.name: Control (task resolution without ChatGPT)
arms.description: Students solved the same tasks with traditional tools, such as paper and pencil, without assistance or external prompts. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 43), Figure 1 and Procedure. The explicit arm total appears only in Figure 1 and is left null under the figure-only rule.

studies.task: Students generated multiple solutions to four open-ended mathematical tasks involving drawing figures of a specified area, measuring marble dispersion, describing water in a tilted prism, and identifying common geometric features (PDF p. 8, printed p. 46, MCT).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (GPT-4o)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 40), Literature review, ChatGPT, names GPT-4o; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 44), Figure 2, visually confirms the ChatGPT 4o model label. Exact snapshot and release year are not stated. The OpenAI citation is a GPT-4 technical report, as shown on PDF p. 20 (printed p. 58), References.

studies.shared_sample: The reconciled screening form flags possible, unconfirmed overlap with c089 (DOI 10.1002/cae.70100), based on matching experimental-arm demographics. c471 does not identify a shared sample. Participant identity has not been established; this flag is carried forward from forms/c471.json, sample_overlap, rather than asserted as a confirmed cross-paper link.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Number of distinct categories of correct answers within each student, summed across the mathematical creativity tasks. Correct solutions were manually classified by independent scorers and disagreements resolved. This is within-person flexibility, not diversity across people. PDF pp. 9-10 (printed pp. 47-48), Mathematical creativity scoring.

open_items: The original randomized total and the number of withdrawals by arm are not reported. Procedure states that students who withdrew were not analyzed and their questionnaires were not collected (PDF p. 4, printed p. 42).

Explicit arm totals appear only in the embedded Figure 1 (PDF p. 5, printed p. 43). Following extraction rule 1, arm counts remain null; Table 2 demographic cells were not summed. A text/table report of arm totals would permit their transcription under this rule.

The randomization mechanism and allocation concealment are not described. The title and abstract call the study quasi-experimental, whereas Procedure explicitly states random assignment (PDF pp. 1 and 4, printed pp. 39 and 42).
The reference pool for originality-category frequencies and exact frequency-band boundaries are not specified (PDF p. 9, printed p. 47, Mathematical creativity scoring).
Scorer qualifications and blinding to condition are not stated (PDF p. 10, printed p. 48, Mathematical creativity scoring).

Table 5 labels its standardized effects d without defining the denominator. ANCOVA results give F tests and partial eta-squared but no adjusted arm means, signed differences, standard errors or confidence intervals (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 49-50).

The exact GPT-4o snapshot and release year are not printed; the literature-review citation points to the GPT-4 technical report rather than a model release statement (PDF p. 2, printed p. 40; PDF p. 20, printed p. 58).
Possible participant overlap with c089 remains unconfirmed, as flagged in the reconciled screening form. Shared-sample status must not be inferred from matching demographic summaries.
notes: Reconciled against the supplied published PDF on 2026-10-11. The entire markdown conversion was read in six contiguous chunks through the final citation. No appendix or separate supplement is present or identified. Every cited PDF page was text-extracted with pymupdf; Table 5 was additionally recovered with find_tables(strategy="text"). Figures 1 and 2 were rendered and inspected in memory without creating files. The diff contains repeated entries for the same estimate/count field; each unique discrepancy is resolved once. There are no estimates exclusive to either extractor. The paper reports three eligible output outcomes, corresponding to all three screening-form outcome IDs and their ChatGPT-versus-control contrasts. Each has an unadjusted t-test record and an ANCOVA record adjusted only for prior ChatGPT experience. These six records represent alternative analyses of three outcomes in the same sample and must not be treated as independent samples. No eligible outcome or contrast was missing from both extractions. The excluded baseline, self-reports, calibration indices, within-arm correlations, nonrandomized covariate effects and process time are listed in not_extracted. The fields on which the extractors agreed were checked independently. The analyzed total is printed in Participants (PDF p. 7, printed p. 45), and no outcome-specific exclusions are reported. Initial allocation totals and withdrawal counts are not reported (PDF p. 4, printed p. 42). Procedure explicitly states random assignment and describes both groups within classroom sessions, supporting lab_rct and individual assignment despite the title's quasi-experimental label (PDF pp. 1 and 4, printed pp. 39 and 42). All eligible outcomes score solutions produced with assigned assistance available, so question is with_ai, outcome_with_ai is true, and timing is immediate. The design compares separate groups, so within_person is null; the paper's within-subject self-efficacy comparison is a self-report and is excluded (PDF pp. 4-6 and 12, printed pp. 42-44 and 50). Flexibility counts categories within a student, fluency counts correct solutions, and originality scores category rarity; these are flexibility, fluency and novelty, respectively, not across-person diversity or a correct-answer convergent test (PDF p. 9, printed p. 47). Each indicator is summed across the tasks for each participant, supporting unit and se_basis participant and sd_level participant for Table 5. Higher scores mean more_creative for flexibility/originality and more_ideas for fluency (PDF pp. 9-11, printed pp. 47-49). Only the pre-assistance baseline combines the three indicators into an overall score. No post-intervention overall-creativity composite, across-person diversity outcome or later unassisted creative output is reported. The intervention includes structured prompting guidance as well as ChatGPT; the control receives neither (PDF pp. 5-7 and 14, printed pp. 43-45 and 52). GPT-4o is named in the literature review and shown in Figure 2, but its release year is not established by the paper; the cited OpenAI report is about GPT-4 (PDF pp. 2, 6 and 20, printed pp. 40, 44 and 58). Under extraction rule 1, per-arm analyzed counts remain null because they appear only in the raster procedure diagram, Figure 1 (PDF p. 5, printed p. 43). Table 2 demographic cells were not summed, and degrees of freedom were not used as participant counts. Figure labels appear in resolutions solely to document why those values were not extracted. All recorded estimate statistics were checked against Table 5 or the ANCOVA text (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 49-50); printed precision is preserved in source quotations. No effects, counts, standard deviations, standard errors, intervals or p-value bounds were calculated. Table 5 prints p = 0.000 for flexibility and fluency; these remain numeric zero with the exact printed values in the quotes. The paper states that both sets of p values use Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. The screening form's open issues concerning randomization details, attrition, originality scoring, scorer qualifications/blinding and possible shared participants remain in open_items. No API lookup or web search was used.
